question: A thin piece of wood of uniform density in the shape of an equilateral triangle with side length \(3\) inches weighs \(12\) ounces. A second piece of the same type of wood, with the same thickness, also in the shape of an equilateral triangle, has side length \(5\) inches. Which of the following is closest to the weight, in ounces, of the second piece?
solution:
The two equilateral triangles are similar, with length scale factor \(5/3\). Both the base and its corresponding height scale by this factor, so their areas have ratio
\[
\frac{\text{second area}}{\text{first area}}
=\left(\frac53\right)^2=\frac{25}{9}.
\]
Equal density and thickness make the weight per square inch the same for both pieces. Consequently, the second piece weighs
\[
12\cdot\frac{25}{9}=\frac{100}{3}
=33\frac13\text{ ounces}.
\]
The closest listed weight is \(33.3\) ounces, choice D.

Contexts such as price, quantity and total, or speed, time and distance, supply familiar examples. Direct proportion can be learned through other contexts like side length and perimeter.
Direct proportion rests on a constant ratio value, which is ratio meaning. Proportion equations matter only when problems are solved by setting up a proportion.

The criteria identify an invariant ratio and use its value to find the other quantity. This requires the quotient meaning of a ratio, without the additional cross-product property of proportions. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: Interpreting the constant ratio and using its value in direct proportion

edges.reason: Similar polygons introduce a common side ratio. The node also covers curved regions and general similarities, so polygon criteria help but are not strictly necessary.
The triangle area-ratio property is a concrete instance of the general square law. The law can be justified by grid or dilation arguments for any region without triangle properties.
edges.scope: triangle special case of the square law

edges.reason: Distinguishing a squared area factor from the linear factor presupposes area as a two-dimensional size, separate from perimeter. Without it, the square law has no meaning.
The scale factor and the area factor are ratios of corresponding quantities. Applying or inverting k^2 needs ratios as quotients, which every method of this node uses.
